significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—"high-surprise, low-teacher-probability tokens recover oracle divergence tokens"—together with form-(ii) causal claims that suppressing those tokens' gradients reduces trait transmission and that early-layer restriction suffices. This establishes both a phenomenon and a mechanism: surprise predicts sparse carrier tokens, while their gradient contributions and early-layer changes explain and control transmission, constraining which tokens and layers future accounts should implicate rather than merely showing that a separable direction exists. The branches are determinate and informative: failure of P1 rules out single-teacher surprise as a sufficient carrier proxy, failure of P2 despite P1 separates carrier identification from causal defensibility, and failure of P3 rejects early-layer sufficiency; the stated adaptive-high-probability-token limitation prevents this from becoming a general law of all subliminal transmission. Topic substitution lowers the assessment materially—the generic topic alone would suggest studying or defending subliminal learning, but not the claim-specific surprise-to-divergence predictive coupling and its separable causal consequences—so the score is supported by the claim rather than the topic's importance.

reach.justification: The named handle is "Divergence-Token Regularization (DTR)," specifically the surprise score "s_i = -log p_teacher(x_i | context)" coupled to gradient down-weighting or an early-layer consistency penalty. It is ex ante rather than post hoc because it is a "training-time immunization" applied while distilling from an untrusted teacher, leaving an action window before the resulting student is deployed. After per-model recalibration, the conclusion would still predict that high-surprise tokens are enriched for divergence carriers and that targeting them offers a favorable suppression-utility tradeoff, while its asserted reach covers several traits and model families but excludes diffuse carriers and adaptive teachers encoding through high-probability tokens; downstream users therefore include practitioners who gate or run third-party distillation, not only interpretability researchers. Topic substitution fails to preserve this score: removing DTR, its measurable surprise proxy, and its pre-deployment intervention leaves only the broad instruction to extend subliminal-learning research, which supplies neither this transferable relation nor a usable handle.
